sentences.text: The insurer is in appeal challenging the compensation of Rs.18,44,400/- awarded for the death of Nagaraj Nayak, who was aged about 19 years.

2. It is the case of the insurer that the deduction towards personal expenses of th from the income of the deceased is incorrect, since the deceased was a bachelor and as a consequence 50% ought to have been deducted towards his personal expenditure.

3. In my view, though there is merit in this argument, having regard to the fact that the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the claimant at Rs.8,000/- per month as against the sum of Rs.11,000/-, as determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and since no amounts are awarded towards 'loss of love and affection', in my view, in the totality of the circumstances, the compensation awarded is just and proper.

It is to be stated here that if the income is re- assessed and the sum of 'loss of love and affection' is added, as this Court is under an obligation to award just compensation, the sums so arrived would more or less, be the same as the present sums are awarded and therefore, this is not a fit case to entertain an appeal.
Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed.

SD/-
(N S SANJAY GOWDA) JUDGE HNM The Manager vs Chikka Krishna Nayak @ Krishna Nayak on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29624527/
